description: Last report time plus the current instant to a three-state presence value and the elapsed silence it was decided from. Boundaries are inclusive-online: exactly 90s is online, exactly 900s is stale. A lastSeen in the future clamps to zero elapsed and reports online, so a peer's clock skew does not look like a local failure.

cases.description: A device that reported five seconds ago is plainly reachable.
One missed 60-second heartbeat is still online: the window tolerates it without requiring a second.
Silence of exactly the online threshold is online, not stale. Pinned here rather than left to whichever comparison operator each implementation happens to use.
One second past the online threshold is stale. Paired with online-exactly-at-threshold to pin the boundary from both sides.
Seven minutes of silence sits well inside the stale band, which is the state a backgrounded phone spends most of its time in.
Silence of exactly the offline threshold is still stale, not offline. The same inclusive rule as the online boundary, so the two boundaries cannot drift apart in style.
One second past the offline threshold is offline. Paired with stale-exactly-at-offline-threshold to pin that boundary from both sides.
A device silent for a full day. The elapsed time is still reported, so the user can tell this apart from one silent for a minute.
A device with no recorded report is offline, and has no age. The absent value must not be treated as the current instant, which would report a device that has never been seen as online.

A peer with a skewed clock reports a lastSeen five seconds ahead of now. Elapsed clamps to zero and the state is online: treating it as an error would make the peer's clock skew look like a local failure.
The same clamp holds for a month of skew, not only for a few seconds. Without this case an implementation could clamp with a small tolerance and still pass.
